items.title: Origin and Anduril Demonstrate Integrated Counter-UAS Solution
items.summary: Origin Robotics and Anduril successfully demonstrated the integration of the Blaze autonomous interceptor with Anduril’s Lattice for Air Defense platform before Latvian military leadership

sections.label: What happened
lines: Origin Robotics and Anduril successfully demonstrated the integration of the Blaze autonomous interceptor with Anduril’s Lattice for Air Defense platform before Latvian military leadership

sections.label: Context
lines: 2022: Origin Robotics is founded in Riga, Latvia, by former consumer-drone entrepreneurs to build autonomous unmanned aerial systems.
2024: Origin Robotics raises €4 million in pre-seed financing, comprising venture capital and grants from the EU and Latvia's Ministry of Defence (Funding, EUR 4 million).
2025: Origin Robotics debuts the Blaze autonomous counter-drone interceptor designed to pursue fast-moving aerial threats like loitering munitions.
6 Feb 2026: Latvian Defense Minister Andris Sprūds announces that Latvia, Estonia, and Belgium have received the first Blaze interceptor systems.
17 Jun 2026: France selects the Blaze autonomous interceptor system following an evaluation by the French DGA, becoming the fourth European NATO member to adopt it.

25 Sep 2026: Origin Robotics and Anduril sign a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) in Los Angeles to explore integrating the Blaze interceptor with Anduril’s Lattice command-and-control platform (Agreement).

31 Oct 2026: Origin and Anduril complete technical integration within four days and successfully demonstrate the combined Blaze and Lattice counter-UAS solution to Latvian military leadership in Latvia.

sections.label: Policy direction
lines: EU — White Paper for European Defence – Readiness 2030 and ReArm Europe Plan (2025-03-19): Close critical capability gaps in seven priority areas (including air and missile defence and artillery) and build a stronger European defence industrial base; ReArm Europe enables over €800 billion of defence spending.

EU — Council Regulation establishing the Security Action for Europe (SAFE) instrument (2025-05-27): Up to €150 billion in EU loans for member states investing in defence industrial production through common procurement of priority capabilities.

sections.label: The bigger picture
lines: Following the 2025 debut of autonomous interceptors and late-2026 integration agreements, counter-UAS development increasingly leverages open software frameworks to rapidly connect disparate effectors and command-and-control systems, signaling a shift toward plug-and-play multi-layer air defense

Origin Robotics depends on Origin Robotics — Onboard Computer Vision & AI Guidance Software.

lines: Business development and engineering teams should note how rapidly open software interfaces enable multi-vendor interoperability for counter-UAS architectures

items.title: NATO integrates counter-drone marketplace into 24/7 air defence architecture
items.summary: NATO launched and integrated a C-UAS marketplace featuring 16 vetted solutions from five suppliers into its revised air and missile defence architecture.

sections.label: What happened
lines: NATO launched and integrated a C-UAS marketplace featuring 16 vetted solutions from five suppliers into its revised air and missile defence architecture.

sections.label: Context
lines: Jun 2023: NATO Allied Command Transformation and member nations expand short-range air defense tests incorporating counter-drone architectures across eastern flank exercises (Testing).
9 Jun 2026: Alta Ares closes a EUR 50 million funding round led by Air Street Capital to scale industrial production of AI-guided counter-drone interceptors across Europe (Funding, EUR 50 million).

7 Jul 2026: Allied leaders formally introduce the "Drone Edge" initiative during the NATO Summit Defence Industry Forum in Ankara, committing over $40 billion toward counter-drone capabilities over five years (USD 40 billion).
17 Sep 2026: Novacium secures its first commercial order for more than 100 AA NOVA silicon-anode battery packs to power Alta Ares interceptor drones.

5 Nov 2026: NATO launches the Counter-Unmanned Aircraft Systems (C-UAS) marketplace managed by the NATO Communications and Information Agency (NCIA) with 16 vetted solutions from five selected suppliers.
6 Nov 2026: Axon reports strategic inventory investments totaling $225 million for 2026 to safeguard counter-drone hardware supply chains against lead-time shocks (USD 225 million).
12 Nov 2026: Allied Air Command integrates the newly established counter-drone marketplace directly into its revised 24/7 air and missile defence operational architecture.

sections.label: The bigger picture
lines: Following years of expanded testing and the $40 billion Drone Edge initiative launched in July 2026, NATO is systematically operationalizing multi-supplier counter-drone frameworks into unified command structures, signaling a permanent shift toward streamlined C-UAS acquisition.

sections.label: Down the supply chain
lines: Interceptor Drones depends on Alta Ares — Edge-AI computing boards and optical tracking sensors (e.g., Pixel Lock vision processing units).
C-UAS Platforms depends on Axon Enterprise (Dedrone) — Multi-sensor command-and-control software layers (DedroneTracker.AI / Dedrone C2).
C-UAS Platforms depends on Echodyne — Counter-drone tactical radars (EchoShield micro-Doppler radar).

United States Federal Government: export licensing on Executive Order 14307 (Unleashing American Drone Dominance): Prioritizes US-made unmanned aircraft systems and enforces strict supply chain security rules regarding subcomponent sourcing from 2025-06-06 (in_force).

sections.label: Why it matters
lines: NCIA‑vetted supplier channels are included in the counter‑drone marketplace that has been integrated into Allied Air Command's operational architecture.

items.title: Saab Unveils Optionally Crewed Combat Boat 90 CX at Euronaval 2026

lines: 1990: Dockstavarvet initiates development and production of the original Stridsbåt 90 H (CB90) fast assault craft for the Swedish Navy.
1991: First units of the CB90 enter commission with the Royal Swedish Navy.
Jun 2017: The Swedish Defence Materiel Administration (FMV) places an order for modernized shrapnel-protected variants designated CB90HSM (Contract).
24 Oct 2019: Saab highlights the operational rollout and performance capabilities of the CB90HSM featuring upgraded Scania DSI13 V8 engines and Trackfire integration.
15 Sep 2024: Sweden announces the transfer of CB90 class fast assault craft to Ukraine to support naval littoral defense operations.
21 Sep 2026: The Finnish Navy integrates coastal and amphibious training units around fast patrol and small combat boat platforms to expand littoral uncrewed concept developments.
12 Nov 2026: Saab officially unveils the CB90 CX at Euronaval 2026 as an optionally crewed, larger evolution of the CB90NG platform.

lines: EU — Preserving Peace – Defence Readiness Roadmap 2030 (2025-10-16): Milestones towards full EU defence readiness by 2030, with four flagships: European Drone Defence Initiative, Eastern Flank Watch, European Air Shield and European Space Shield.

lines: From the initial 1990 development of the CB90 by Dockstavarvet and subsequent operational deployments, regional naval forces like Finland and Sweden have progressively evolved fast combat craft toward uncrewed concepts and distributed littoral operations; signal: accelerating adoption of autonomous small-boat architectures for Baltic defense.

items.title: EIC Scaling Club companies cross €4B in funding, outpacing peers
items.summary: A new performance report shows that EIC Scaling Club portfolio companies have raised more than €4 billion, with 56 percent securing post-joining investments averaging €60.6 million.

sections.label: What happened
lines: A new performance report shows that EIC Scaling Club portfolio companies have raised more than €4 billion, with 56 percent securing post-joining investments averaging €60.6 million.

sections.label: Context
lines: 19 Mar 2024: The European Commission announces the creation of the EIC Scaling Club to foster European deeptech unicorns.
Oct 2024: The EIC Scaling Club introduces its second cohort, expanding the portfolio to 120 companies across Europe.
20 Oct 2024: The EIC launches the Trusted Investors Network at the EIC Scaling Summit to mobilize co-investments for deeptech scale-ups.
4 Nov 2026: The EIC Scaling Club publishes its performance report showing cumulative funding crossing €4 billion, growing 2.3 times faster than control peers (EUR 4 billion).

sections.label: The bigger picture
lines: Since the 2024 launch of the EIC Scaling Club and its subsequent portfolio expansion to 120 companies, targeted public co-investments and initiatives like the Trusted Investors Network have helped scale cumulative funding past €4 billion by late 2026, signaling a major push for European technological sovereignty.

items.title: UK joins Norway’s P1118 vessel program for Royal Navy motherships
items.summary: The UK Ministry of Defence announced a £90 million commitment to join Norway's P1118 Standardised Vessel Programme, acquiring three Offshore Support Vessels with the first scheduled for delivery in 2031.

sections.label: What happened
lines: The UK Ministry of Defence announced a £90 million commitment to join Norway's P1118 Standardised Vessel Programme, acquiring three Offshore Support Vessels with the first scheduled for delivery in 2031.

sections.label: Context
lines: Dec 2025: UK and Norway sign the wider Lunna House Agreement, setting the stage for industrial and naval cooperation including prospective UK integration into Norway’s vessel programmes (Agreement).
22 Jan 2026: Norwegian Defence Materiel Agency (NDMA) initiates prequalification for the P1118 design competition covering up to 28 modular vessels.
30 Mar 2026: NDMA selects Kongsberg Defence & Aerospace and Salt Ship Design consortium to develop the concept and basic design for the P1118 standardised platform family.

20 Oct 2026: NDMA signals market prequalification rules for the ocean-going variant of P1118, confirming an initial procurement scope comprising up to 20 hulls total for Norway, the UK (up to six), and Lithuania.
11 Nov 2026: Thales UK and Kongsberg sign an MoU for anti-submarine warfare (ASW) solutions aimed at future uncrewed surface vessel configurations (Agreement).

12 Nov 2026: UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting and Norwegian State Secretary Tore O. Sandvik formally announce the UK’s commitment to join the P1118 programme for three vessels (plus three options) at the Atlantic Future Forum in Oslo (GBP 90 million).
2031: Contractual delivery date scheduled for the first Royal Navy Offshore Support Vessel (Plan).

sections.label: The bigger picture
lines: Following the December 2025 Lunna House Agreement and subsequent P1118 design milestones by Kongsberg and Salt Ship Design, bilateral naval procurement is expanding into joint standardized modular platforms across allied nations, underpinned by growing industrial cooperation like the Thales UK-Kongsberg ASW MoU.

sections.label: Down the supply chain
lines: Naval Platform Integration & Combat Management Systems depends on Kongsberg Defence & Aerospace (Norway) — Sole-source provider of core command, control, and combat system architectures for the P1118 vessel family.
Vessel Concept & Naval Architecture depends on Salt Ship Design AS (Norway) — Principal designer responsible for basic platform engineering and modular layouts.

sections.label: Why it matters
lines: Defense contractors and supply chain partners in anti-submarine warfare and autonomous mine countermeasures should align their integration strategies with the standardized Kongsberg and Salt Ship Design architectures chosen for the P1118 platform family.

items.summary: Diehl Metall and Diehl Defence officially inaugurated a new 155mm shell body production line at Röthenbach an der Pegnitz in cooperation with Nammo AS.

sections.label: What happened
lines: Diehl Metall and Diehl Defence officially inaugurated a new 155mm shell body production line at Röthenbach an der Pegnitz in cooperation with Nammo AS.

sections.label: Context
lines: 2019: Diehl Defence and Nammo AS establish the ARGE DiNa joint working group geared towards the German ammunition market.
Jul 2023: BAAINBw concludes an initial framework agreement with ARGE DiNa covering up to 350,000 155mm artillery shells (Agreement).
Jun 2024: Diehl launches the industrial project to convert a 7,000-square-meter facility at Röthenbach an der Pegnitz following a major call-off.
9 Jul 2024: BAAINBw and ARGE DiNa sign a substantially expanded framework contract and a major initial call-off order (Contract).
Oct 2026: Pilot-series production commences at the newly converted Röthenbach plant utilizing two new forging presses.
10 Nov 2026: Diehl Metall and Diehl Defence officially inaugurate the new 155mm shell body production line in cooperation with Nammo AS.

sections.label: Policy direction
lines: EU — White Paper for European Defence – Readiness 2030 and ReArm Europe Plan (2025-03-19): Close critical capability gaps in seven priority areas (including air and missile defence and artillery) and build a stronger European defence industrial base; ReArm Europe enables over €800 billion of defence spending.

sections.label: The bigger picture
lines: Following the 2019 establishment of ARGE DiNa and subsequent framework contracts, European defence industrial expansion under the ReArm Europe plan continues to address critical artillery capability gaps.

sections.label: Down the supply chain
lines: 155 mm Steel Shell Bodies depends on Diehl Metall (Röthenbach, Germany) — Forged and machined using two new heavy forging presses and specialized metal-forming infrastructure.
High-Explosive (HE) Filling & Integration depends on Diehl Defence.
Projectile Technology & Design depends on Nammo AS (Norway) — Core technical design, engineering data, and production know-how transferred from Nammo AS.

sections.label: Why it matters
lines: Procurement and supply chain professionals should monitor these expanded domestic manufacturing capacities for upcoming 155mm ammunition call-offs.

11 Nov 2026: The Australian Government formally announced the milestone achievement of first steel cutting for the LCH programme alongside parallel LCM construction progress.

items.title: U.S. Seeks Formal Russian Proposals on European Security Architecture
items.summary: U.S. negotiators officially asked Moscow to table a formal written proposal detailing its terms for a future European security treaty.

sections.label: What happened
lines: U.S. negotiators officially asked Moscow to table a formal written proposal detailing its terms for a future European security treaty.

sections.label: Context
lines: 28 May 2002: Establishment of the NATO-Russia Council at the Rome Summit to serve as a mechanism for consensus, cooperation, and joint consultation.
Jun 2026: U.S. diplomatic channels initiate back-channel exploratory talks with Russian representatives regarding post-conflict parameters in Eastern Europe.
5 Nov 2026: President Donald Trump meets Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev in Washington, signalling a willingness to negotiate broader continental security architectures.
6 Nov 2026: European capitals express acute concern and surprise over potential backroom bargains bypassing EU and frontline state sovereignty.
7 Nov 2026: Senior NATO officials and European diplomatic advisers hold emergency briefings in Brussels to counter potential U.S. concessions on alliance force posture in Eastern Europe.
10 Nov 2026: Trilateral U.S.-Ukraine-Russia peace talks commence in Abu Dhabi, expanded to include national security advisers from France, Germany, the UK, and EU/NATO representatives.
11 Nov 2026: U.S. negotiators officially ask Moscow to table a formal written proposal detailing its terms for a future European security treaty, reviving fears of constraints on NATO expansion.

sections.label: Policy direction
lines: US — 2026 National Defense Strategy (2026-01-23): Four lines of effort: defend the homeland (including Golden Dome missile defence), deter China in the Indo-Pacific, more burden-sharing by allies, and supercharge the US defence industrial base.

US — PAC-3 MSE framework agreement under the Acquisition Transformation Strategy (2026-01-06): Seven-year framework agreements for proven munitions, giving industry long-term demand so it invests in capacity; PAC-3 MSE output to rise from about 600 to about 2,000 a year, subject to Congress.

sections.label: The bigger picture
lines: Following back-channel talks initiated in June 2026 and President Donald Trump's meeting with Russian envoy Kirill Dmitriev in November 2026, trilateral talks commenced in Abu Dhabi, culminating in requests for formal Russian security proposals; signal: potential realignment of continental security frameworks.

sections.label: Why it matters
lines: Defence industry business development and procurement professionals must monitor potential shifts in NATO force posture and alliance requirements.

items.title: Ukraine War Restores Industrial Warfare to Europe

lines: Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine initiated a prolonged war of attrition that heavily consumed munitions and restored the critical importance of defence production and logistics.

sections.label: Context
lines: 20 Feb 2014: Russia’s illegal annexation of Crimea and initial intervention in the Donbas expose early warning signs of conventional friction in Europe, prompting the NATO Wales Summit Readiness Action Plan.
24 Feb 2022: Russia launches its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, immediately triggering intense attritional artillery exchanges that exhaust Western peacetime munitions stockpiles within weeks.
3 May 2023: The European Commission adopts the Act in Support of Ammunition Production (ASAP) to urgently ramp up EU manufacturing capacities for artillery shells and powders (EUR 500 million).

15 Oct 2025: The European Commission officially launches the European Defence Readiness Roadmap 2030 to bridge persistent implementation gaps in ammunition and heavy weapons manufacturing.

sections.label: What happened
lines: Diehl Defence officially opened a new 7,000 square metre production line in Röthenbach, Germany, for DiNa 155mm artillery shell bodies following an investment in the mid double-digit millions of euros. The project builds on the ARGE DiNa joint venture established by Diehl Defence and Nammo in 2019, with Diehl Metal Forgings manufacturing the shell bodies and Nammo providing design and technology expertise.

sections.label: Context
lines: 2019: Diehl Defence and Nammo established the ARGE DiNa joint venture to serve the German market with DiNa 155mm artillery rounds.
Jun 2024: The project to convert a production hall at Röthenbach for DiNa shell body manufacturing began.
Oct 2026: Pilot production started on the new 7,000 square metre production line following an investment in the mid double-digit millions of euros.
10 Nov 2026: Diehl Defence officially opened the new production line for DiNa 155mm artillery shell bodies in Röthenbach, Germany.

sections.label: Policy direction
lines: EU — White Paper for European Defence – Readiness 2030 and ReArm Europe Plan (2025-03-19): Close critical capability gaps in seven priority areas (including air and missile defence and artillery) and build a stronger European defence industrial base; ReArm Europe enables over €800 billion of defence spending.

sections.label: The bigger picture
lines: Following the establishment of the ARGE DiNa joint venture in January 2019 and the launch of the conversion project in June 2024, pilot production began in October 2026 and culminated in the opening of the new line in November 2026, aligning with EU objectives to close critical artillery gaps and strengthen the European defence industrial base.

sections.label: Context

lines: US — 2026 National Defense Strategy (2026-01-23): Four lines of effort: defend the homeland (including Golden Dome missile defence), deter China in the Indo-Pacific, more burden-sharing by allies, and supercharge the US defence industrial base.

items.title: C4ADS tracks Russian arms shipments to African logistics hubs

items.title: Pentagon Lacks Visibility Over F-35 Spares
items.summary: The GAO confirmed that the Pentagon still lacks visibility over millions of F-35 spare parts and fails to locate previously missing stock.

sections.label: What happened
lines: The GAO confirmed that the Pentagon still lacks visibility over millions of F-35 spare parts and fails to locate previously missing stock.

sections.label: Context
lines: 12 Apr 2019: Initial GAO audits highlight mounting transparency and logistics gaps in the F-35 sustainment supply chain.
15 Mar 2022: GAO reports that the Enterprise Logistics Management System (ELMS) fails to interface with prime contractor property systems.
24 May 2023: GAO reveals that a prime contractor lost over 1 million F-35 spare parts worth $85 million between 2018 and 2022 (USD 85 million).
Dec 2025: Quarterly Contractor Data Requirements List (CDRL) data shows extensive anomalies, including 6% of records priced at $0.01 or less.
31 Mar 2026: Joint spares pool reaches approximately 26 million parts valued at $31 billion, with 17,000 parts worth up to $2.5 billion missing from official property tracking (USD 31 billion).
15 Jul 2026: U.S. Air Force awards Lockheed Martin a $1.6 billion contract for additional spare parts (Contract, USD 1.6 billion).
9 Nov 2026: GAO releases report GAO-27-108713 confirming the Pentagon still lacks visibility over millions of parts and has failed to locate the pre-2023 missing stock.

sections.label: The bigger picture
lines: Since initial 2019 audits highlighted transparency gaps, recurring issues like unlinked contractor property systems in 2022 and millions of missing parts in 2026 demonstrate persistent inventory tracking failures Signal: systemic lack of real-time asset accountability.

sections.label: Down the supply chain
lines: F-35 Global Joint Spares Pool depends on tires, valves, fasteners, structural panels — Comprehensive inventory of 26 million components shared across U.S. services and international operators.
ITAR / EAR: export licensing on F-35 components global transit and repair loop (in_force).

sections.label: Why it matters
lines: Defense contractors and supply chain managers must improve inventory interface systems and data quality to address persistent DoD asset tracking deficits.

items.title: GAO: Over 1M F-35 Parts Still Missing
items.summary: A GAO report released on Nov. 9, 2026, revealed that more than 1 million F-35 spare parts remain missing and 26 million parts across 700 facilities lack real-time oversight.

sections.label: What happened
lines: A GAO report released on Nov. 9, 2026, revealed that more than 1 million F-35 spare parts remain missing and 26 million parts across 700 facilities lack real-time oversight.

sections.label: Context
lines: 30 Sep 2019: Pentagon financial audits reveal chronic systemic inability to track government property and inventory within major weapon systems like the F-35.

Oct 2020: JPO initiates targeted physical inventories across contractor- and government-managed facilities, spending upwards of $17,000,000 USD through fiscal 2025 without achieving accurate tracking (USD 17 million).
23 May 2023: GAO publishes report GAO-23-106098 revealing that over 1 million spare parts worth at least $85,000,000 USD went missing over a five-year window (USD 85 million).
30 Sep 2025: Department of Defense financial statement compilation results in an unquantifiable material misstatement due to untraceable F-35 component assets.

31 Mar 2026: GAO audit cut-off establishes that roughly 17,000 parts worth $1.3 billion to $2.5 billion in maintenance/repair are missing from official inventory systems, and the 1 million previously flagged parts remain unlocated (USD 1.3 billion).
23 Jul 2026: Pentagon awards major F-35 spare parts acquisition contracts to support global fleet requirements (Contract).
9 Nov 2026: GAO releases report GAO-27-108713 stating that more than 1 million F-35 spare parts remain missing and 26 million parts across 700 facilities lack real-time oversight (USD 31 billion).

sections.label: The bigger picture
lines: Since 2019 financial audits have highlighted a chronic inability to track F-35 inventory, leading to unquantifiable material misstatements by September 2025 and ongoing tracking failures through late 2026.

sections.label: Down the supply chain
lines: F-35 Global Spares Pool depends on 26 million components managed across 700+ facilities globally.
F-35 Propulsion System depends on Pratt & Whitney F135 turbofan engine modules and hardware.
Avionics and Electronic Warfare Components depends on Integrated core processors, sensors, and distributed aperture system parts.
United States Government: export licensing on Sensitive stealth components (such as canopy assemblies and radar-absorbent materials) (in_force).

sections.label: Why it matters
lines: Defense contractors and supply chain managers must prepare for stricter integration between enterprise logistics systems and contractor property management infrastructure.

items.title: GAO report highlights record gaps in $31 billion of F-35 parts
items.summary: A GAO report revealed systemic record gaps and inaccurate property tracking across $31 billion in F-35 spare parts.

sections.label: What happened
lines: A GAO report revealed systemic record gaps and inaccurate property tracking across $31 billion in F-35 spare parts.

sections.label: Context
lines: 30 Sep 2019: Department of Defense financial auditors first flag a persistent material weakness regarding the F-35 program's accountable property records.
Oct 2020: The F-35 Joint Program Office begins a series of physical inventory counts, eventually spending at least $17 million through fiscal 2025.
25 May 2023: GAO reports that one prime contractor had recorded losses involving over 1 million F-35 parts valued at more than $85 million.
30 Sep 2025: Pentagon annual financial statements omit key F-35 parts, resulting in an unquantifiable material misstatement identified by auditors.

31 Mar 2026: Audit data shows approximately 17,000 parts in maintenance or repair (valued between $1.3 billion and $2.5 billion) are absent from official property records, while older missing losses remain unresolved.
9 Nov 2026: GAO publishes GAO-27-108713 detailing systemic record gaps across $31 billion in F-35 spare parts.

sections.label: The bigger picture
lines: Since financial auditors first flagged material weaknesses in 2019, property record discrepancies have persisted through successive physical inventories and financial statement omissions, pointing toward prolonged difficulties in achieving clean audit compliance.

sections.label: Down the supply chain
lines: F-35 depends on Lockheed Martin Aeronautics primary structural assemblies and low-observable skin panels — Airframe Integration & Assembly.

U.S. Department of State Directorate of Defense Trade Controls: export licensing on International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) / Export Administration Regulations (EAR): Strict export controls govern all technical data, maintenance manuals, and line-replaceable units (LRUs) across the global F-35 user pool. (in_force).

sections.label: Why it matters
lines: Defense contractors and supply chain personnel must prepare for heightened scrutiny, stricter loss-monitoring procedures, and improved data integration requirements across F-35 maintenance networks.

items.title: Kratos updates Valkyrie baseline unit pricing to $6M-$8M
items.summary: Kratos CEO Eric DeMarco announced during the Q3 2026 earnings call that baseline unit pricing for Valkyrie drones now ranges from $6 million to $8 million depending on configuration, excluding mission systems.

sections.label: What happened
lines: Kratos CEO Eric DeMarco announced during the Q3 2026 earnings call that baseline unit pricing for Valkyrie drones now ranges from $6 million to $8 million depending on configuration, excluding mission systems.

sections.label: Context
lines: Jul 2016: Low Cost Attritable Strike Demonstrator (LCASD) contract awarded by the Air Force Research Laboratory to Kratos (Contract).
14 Mar 2023: U.S. Marine Corps received the first of two XQ-58A unmanned aerial systems for the PAACK-P program.
3 Oct 2023: Marine Corps XQ-58A successfully completed its first test flight at Eglin Air Force Base under the PAACK-P initiative.
Mar 2024: Kratos reported unit price ranges between $4 million (at a scale of 100 airframes) and $6 million for RATO variants.
Sep 2025: Unidentified international customer took delivery of operational Valkyrie drones during the third quarter (Delivered).
12 Oct 2026: The Airbus-Kratos co-developed U740 variant (European Valkyrie bid for the Luftwaffe) achieved its first flight in northern Europe (Testing).
10 Nov 2026: Kratos updated baseline unit pricing to $6 million – $8 million per airframe depending on configuration.

sections.label: The bigger picture
lines: Since the initial 2016 development contract and 2019 maiden flight, the Valkyrie program has progressed through U.S. service testing, international deliveries in 2025, and the October 2026 maiden flight of the European U740 variant, pointing toward expanding serial production.

sections.label: Down the supply chain
lines: None depends on Kratos Defense & Security Solutions (Oklahoma City manufacturing facility) — Airframe structures & composite parts.

U.S. Government: export licensing on International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) and Export Administration Regulations (EAR): Controlled under U.S. Munitions List (USML) categories governing military uncrewed aerial systems, advanced composite structures, and tactical autonomous software (in_force).

sections.label: Why it matters
lines: Defense procurement professionals should factor these updated airframe costs into Collaborative Combat Aircraft budget planning and supply chain forecasting.

items.title: Belgium Selects Thales GM200 MM/C Radar for Blue Dome Air Defence
items.summary: Thales announced that Belgium selected the GM200 MM/C radar to support the Blue Dome air defence programme, providing tracking for drones, missiles, and artillery threats. The radar will integrate with Kongsberg fire distribution centers and Raytheon AMRAAM missiles within the NASAMS architecture.

sections.label: What happened
lines: Thales announced that Belgium selected the GM200 MM/C radar to support the Blue Dome air defence programme, providing tracking for drones, missiles, and artillery threats. The radar will integrate with Kongsberg fire distribution centers and Raytheon AMRAAM missiles within the NASAMS architecture.

sections.label: Context
lines: 20 May 2016: Thales Deutschland and Thales Nederland first demonstrated the GM200 MM/C prototype in integrated fire-control architectures, confirming its performance as a medium-range sensor (Testing).

Dec 2019: The Netherlands ordered the Ground Master 200 Multi-Mission Compact (GM200 MM/C) radars from Thales Nederland to modernise its army's ground-based air surveillance and multi-mission radar capabilities.
3 Jan 2024: Lithuania and the Netherlands signed a joint procurement agreement for Lithuania to acquire Thales GM200 MM/C radar systems produced by Thales Nederland (Agreement, EUR 126.7 million).
14 Feb 2024: Thales Nederland officially delivered the very first serial-production GM200 MM/C radar unit to the Royal Netherlands Army (Delivered).
2 Nov 2026: Lithuania received its first operational Thales GM200 MM/C multifunction radar system to strengthen its national division's artillery location and counter-drone capabilities.

9 Nov 2026: Belgium officially launched the Blue Dome programme at the Royal Military Academy, reactivating the 51st Air Defense Squadron and placing a major order for 20 Rheinmetall Skyranger 30 systems alongside NASAMS batteries (EUR 3.1 billion).
10 Nov 2026: Thales officially announced that Belgium selected the GM200 MM/C radar to form the core sensor network for the Blue Dome air defence system.

sections.label: Policy direction
lines: EU — White Paper for European Defence – Readiness 2030 and ReArm Europe Plan (2025-03-19): Close critical capability gaps in seven priority areas (including air and missile defence and artillery) and build a stronger European defence industrial base; ReArm Europe enables over €800 billion of defence spending.

EU — Council Regulation establishing the Security Action for Europe (SAFE) instrument (2025-05-27): Up to €150 billion in EU loans for member states investing in defence industrial production through common procurement of priority capabilities.

sections.label: The bigger picture
lines: Following initial prototype demonstrations in 2016 and Dutch and Lithuanian procurements between 2019 and 2024, European nations are adopting the GM200 MM/C radar system, which can simplify training and maintenance through commonality.

sections.label: Down the supply chain
lines: None depends on None.

sections.label: Why it matters
lines: Belgium’s decision to use the GM200 MM/C radar contributes to a common air‑defence architecture shared by several European nations.
